references.text: Moses had previously demanded that the entire people, including children, be allowed to go to celebrate a festival for the Lord. Here the demand is expanded to include the livestock.
Pharaoh finally ends up sending the Israelites away with both small and large cattle, just as Moses demanded.
God had promised that the people would serve him on this mountain. Moses did not know exactly what would be required before they arrived there.
Pharaoh finally gives permission to go and serve the Lord, as Moses insisted.
The livestock taken from Egypt was large in number and was later mentioned in connection with settling in the land.
Moses had previously explained that the Israelites' sacrifices would be abhorrent to the Egyptians, so they had to go out to offer them.
Both verses explicitly link 'service' to God's face with concrete sacrificial offerings and livestock, emphasizing that this is the foundation of Israel's identity as God's people.
